text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Government's planned reform of financial support to regions must be postponed for a year because of an earlier agreement with the European Union, which officials "forgot."

- Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said it seems decision on membership of European Economic and Monetary Union could be made by a simple majority in parliament -- and separately from other legislation needed for EMU.
- State auditors say they are concerned about status of parliamentarism, see danger of political power sliding into hands of civil service elite.
- Helsinki Stock Exchange managing director Juhani Erma 50 years old today.
- Alcohol-related illnesses and alcohol poisoning killed 1,202 Finns last year in population of five million. Drink a significant cause of death among men aged 45-54.
- Norwegian Kvaerner's Masa Yards and Kvaerner Kleven plan to compete against Finnyards for contract to build
new icebreaker for Finland.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Money counterfeiting has risen sharply in Finland in past four years. Counterfeiters prefer the dollar.
- Businessman Anders Wiklof, of largely autonomous Aland Islands, says preservation of tax-free alcohol sales in Aland shipping of great importance.
- Postipankki chief economist said it would be better for firms to go into EMU with strong balance sheets than to make showy investments now.
DEMARI
- Metal workers union head Per-Erik Lundh warns against talk about new round of collective wage talks while existing contract still in force.
- Nordic countries divided over timetable to liberalise duty-free alcohol import rules to satisfy EU.
TURUN SANOMAT

- Merita bank CEO Vesa Vainio said banking sector will consolidate with or without EMU -- said Scandinavian cooperation would be first on Merita's list, but that a large European bank could also seek foothold in Finland.
AAMULEHTI
- Merita fund executive Maarit Nakyva says Finnish listed companies' combined profit likely to grow by four billion markka next year to 19.43 billion.
